fact: INE president said the pilot census in Magude, run from 1 Aug 2026 at a cost of EUR 372,900, closed on 21 Aug 2026 and the digital system will be improved before the first digital census planned for 2027.

A pilot census was launched on 1 Aug 2026 in Magude district (177 enumeration areas, 177 enumerators, 38 controllers, about USD 430,000) ahead of the fifth general census of 2027; World Bank initial financing of USD 12.7m and a USD 68m gap of USD 110m were reported.
INE's estimate cites the last census in 2017 as having recorded just over 26 million inhabitants; no enumeration date is given.

Training of 260 candidates (216 to be selected: 178 enumerators, 38 controllers) was launched on 27 Jul 2026 in Magude for the census pilot of 1-15 Aug, ahead of the fifth census scheduled for 2027.
The record states a population and housing census was conducted during 2017, with data to be processed in 2018 and 2019 (Sida SEK 40m support via UNFPA); no exact dates.
Sida committed SEK 25,000,000 (US$2.96m) on 2015-12-01 to co-finance Mozambique's 2017 population census, with the government allocating 367.5 million meticais for 2015 and enumeration set for 2017.
INE's national planning meeting of 9-10 September 2026 in Maputo put the operational preparation of the 2027 Population and Housing Census at the centre of its agenda.
